'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2023 attacks on U.S. bases in Iraq and Syria]]
**[[United States Armed Forces|United States forces]] are attacked three times in the past 24 hours in [[Iraq]], including [[Drone warfare|drone strikes]] on [[Al-Asad Airbase]] and [[Al-Harir Air Base]], and an [[Improvised explosive device|IED]] attack on a U.S. patrol near the [[Mosul Dam]]. No casualties are reported. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/drone-explosive-attacks-target-us-forces-across-iraq-sources-2023-11-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***An unidentified [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] strikes a building in the port city of [[Eilat]], after [[Israel]] intercepts a [[ballistic missile]] over the [[Red Sea]] with its [[Arrow (missile family)|Arrow missile defense system]]. The [[Yemen]]-based [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] claim responsibility, but the [[Israel Defense Forces]] blame an unspecified organization in [[Syria]] for the strike. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-military-says-unidentified-drone-hits-southern-city-eilat-2023-11-09/ (Reuters)]
**[[October-November 2023 Jenin incursion]]
***Israeli forces use [[bulldozer]]s to destroy streets in [[Jenin]] in the West Bank, supported by helicopters and [[reconnaissance]] aircraft, following a [[shootout]] in the city that killed 15 [[Palestinians]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/nov/09/nine-palestinians-killed-by-israeli-forces-in-west-bank-daytime-raid (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Jabalia refugee camp airstrikes]]
***At least 30 [[Palestinians]] are killed in [[Israeli Air Force|Israeli]] [[airstrike]]s overnight in the [[Jabalia refugee camp]] and in the [[Sabra, Gaza|Sabra]] neighborhood in [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/9/israel-gaza-war-live-day-34 (Al Jazeera)]
**Three [[human rights]] organisations, [[Al Haq]], [[Al Mezan]], and the [[Palestinian Centre for Human Rights]], file a [[lawsuit]] with the [[International Criminal Court]] calling for the court to consider [[Crime of apartheid|apartheid]] and [[genocide]] in its [[International Criminal Court investigation in Palestine|investigation of the ongoing situation in Palestine]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/9/three-rights-groups-file-icc-lawsuit-against-israel-over-gaza-genocide (Al Jazeera)]
**The heads of the [[UNRWA]] and the [[World Health Organization]] say that conditions at [[Al-Shifa hospital]], Gaza's largest hospital, are "disastrous" with [[emergency room]]s overflowing with sick and injured patients. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/9/israel-gaza-war-live-day-34 (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[Indonesia Hospital]] in northern Gaza reports at least 65 deaths and more than 100 injuries from ongoing [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] bombardment. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/9/israel-gaza-war-live-day-34 (Al Jazeera)]
**At least three people are killed and dozens more are injured when an [[Israel]]i airstrike hits near the Al-Nasr Hospital in western Gaza. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/9/israel-gaza-war-live-day-34 (Al Jazeera)]
**At least four people are killed and dozens more  are injured by Israeli [[artillery]] fire and [[shell (projectile)|shelling]] in southern Gaza. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/9/israel-gaza-war-live-day-34 (Al Jazeera)]
**Two [[Israeli settlers]] are shot, and one is seriously injured, near the [[West Bank]] settlement of [[Itamar (settlement)|Itamar]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/9/israel-gaza-war-live-day-34 (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Mohammad Barakeh]], the head of the [[High Follow-Up Committee for Arab Citizens of Israel]], is arrested by Israeli forces in [[Nazareth]] for planning a [[2023 Israel–Hamas war protests|protest against the war]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1787819/israeli-forces-arrest-mohammad-barakeh-other-palestinian-politicians (Dawn)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/11/9/israel-gaza-war-live-day-34 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Operation 1027]]
***[[Myanmar]] [[state media]] reports that [[Tatmadaw]]-installed [[President of Myanmar|president]] [[Myint Swe]] expressed concern that the country will be divided into multiple parts if the success of the rebel [[offensive (military)|offensive]] continues, as hundreds of soldiers are killed during the offensive. [https://www.barrons.com/news/armed-rebellion-risks-break-up-of-myanmar-junta-backed-president-573f05ed (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
***[[Three Brotherhood Alliance|Rebel forces]] capture the [[Townships of Myanmar|township]] capitals of [[Namhkam, Shan State|Namhkam]] and [[Kunlong]] in [[Shan State]]. [https://burma.irrawaddy.com/news/2023/11/07/376163.html (Irrawaddy)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Air pollution in Lahore]]
**Toxic gray [[smog]] causes tens of thousands of people in [[Lahore]], [[Pakistan]], to become ill, forcing [[Government of Punjab, Pakistan|authorities]] to close schools, markets, and parks for four days. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-smog-school-markets-shut-pollution-2b752ee29d1be2b8c93ec8bd5a81bf62 (AP)]
*[[Puerto Rico]] declares an [[influenza]] [[epidemic]] after 25,900 cases have been reported since July, with 42 deaths and more than 900 hospitalizations. [https://apnews.com/article/puerto-rico-flu-epidemic-0a9dda2ac3b407486d44412f6cbc62e0 (AP)]
*The [[U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] approves the world's first [[Chikungunya vaccine|vaccine]] against the [[chikungunya]] virus. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2682373/us-approves-first-vaccine-against-chikungunya-virus-drug-regulator (AFP via ''Bangkok Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Kazakhstan relations]]
**[[Kazatomprom]], the world's largest [[uranium]] producer, and the [[China Uranium Corporation]] reach a long-term agreement for the supply of [[natural uranium]] concentrate to [[China]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2023/11/09/Kazakhstan-strikes-deal-with-China-to-supply-uranium (AFP via Al Arabiya)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Murder of Ashling Murphy]]
**The [[High Court (Ireland)|High Court]] of [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] convicts [[Slovaks|Slovak]] man Jozef Puška of Ashling Murphy's murder. Puška faces a [[mandatory life sentence]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/11/11/world/americas-emea/slovak-convicted-of-teacher-murder-that-shook-ireland/1919157 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Suhartoyo]] is elected to become [[Chief Justice of the Constitutional Court of Indonesia]] replacing [[Anwar Usman]], following the Honor Council's decision to remove Usman from his position. This decision follows a controversial ruling regarding the age limit for presidential and [[Vice President of Indonesia|vice-presidential]] [[candidate]]s. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/constitutional-court-appoints-suhartoyo-as-new-chief-justice (''Jakarta Globe'')]
*[[Spanish politician]] [[Alejo Vidal-Quadras Roca]] is shot in the face while walking in [[Madrid]], [[Spain]], and taken to hospital in critical condition. [https://nos.nl/artikel/2497223-politicus-in-spanje-neergeschoten-vermoedelijk-gerichte-aanslag (NOS)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**A spokesperson for [[UK]] [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Rishi Sunak]] says  [[United Kingdom]] [[Home Secretary]] [[Suella Braverman]] made unauthorized comments, after she doubles down on referring to pro-Palestinian demonstrations as “mobs” and “[[hate crimes|hate marches]]”. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/9/calls-to-sack-uks-braverman-grow-after-comments-on-pro-palestinian (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2023 Spanish government formation]]
**[[Prime Minister of Spain|Spanish Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]] agrees to an [[amnesty]] deal with the [[Catalan independence movement|Catalan separatist]] [[Together for Catalonia (2020)|Together for Catalonia]] party in order to secure the necessary support for another term in office. The agreement causes protests in [[Madrid]] with the [[right-wing]] [[People's Party (Spain)|People's Party]] calling it a "humiliation" for [[Spain|the country]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-67368314 (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Videotelephony|Video chat]] site [[Omegle]], which allowed users to have anonymous one-on-one conversations with strangers, shuts down after 14 years due to criticism by U.S. authorities of failing to block [[sexual predator|predatory users]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/omegle-shut-down-1.7023708 (CBC)] [https://apnews.com/article/omegle-chat-app-shutdown-online-abuse-603130f8071085fb313428fd027f0cf0 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-67364634 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*The [[Guinness World Records]] and the [[World Surf League]] confirm that [[Surfing in Australia|Australian surfer]] [[Laura Enever]] has set a new [[List of surfing records|surfing record]] for the largest wave ever [[Surfing#Maneuvers|paddled]] into by a woman, with a 13.3-metre (44-foot) wave surfed in [[Hawaii]], U.S., on January 22, surpassing [[Surfing in the United States|American surfer]] [[Andrea Moller]]'s previous record. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/11/09/sport/laura-enever-world-record-surfer-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
